sentences.text: Rothia mucilaginosa is described as an oral commensal that is relatively abundant in the lungs of patients with cystic fibrosis.

Studies have reported anti-inflammatory properties for it in three-dimensional lung epithelial cell cultures and mouse models relevant to chronic lung diseases, and it has also been associated with severe infections.

In bronchoalveolar lavage fluid from patients with pulmonary infections, R. mucilaginosa was enriched in patients without acute respiratory distress syndrome, and its culture supernatant protected mice in a model.
Draft metagenome-assembled genomes of six R. mucilaginosa strains have been recovered from the oral microbiome of distinct human subjects.
